decisions.reason: The requirement still applies to every board and component; reducing the board count does not change its mounting or drop-retention rule.
The one-board decision does not change the required sensor air inlet or outlet locations.
The source does not change the display cutout, mounting, connection, installation, or unresolved display-size requirements.
The board-count change does not alter either permitted enclosure light-path method.
The enclosure must remain easy to assemble regardless of the reduced board count.
The source retains buttons and does not change their connectors, GPIO mappings, reset wiring, touch inputs, or panel power-button behavior.
An existing message-843 MODIFY already records that the separate power board is absent and removes its obsolete mechanical-layout attributes.
An existing message-843 MODIFY already records that the separate sensor board is absent and removes its obsolete board-layout attributes.

The existing message-843 MODIFY already removes the obsolete multiboard orientation, alignment, cable-path, board-order, and connector-access constraints; the source does not necessarily invalidate the remaining layout attributes.
The existing message-843 MODIFY already captures the accepted connector distribution for the one-board layout, subject to the previously stated edge and antenna constraints.

The single-board decision makes the old reference to an absent power board potentially stale, but the source does not establish whether USB activation, LDO selection, or powered scope changes after power circuitry is integrated.
Moving from separate power, main, and sensor boards to one board eliminates interboard destinations and sensor-board links, making the old aggregate JST count and destination inventory stale.

source_message.text: Yes, I think that should be possible. With only one board plus sensors, buttons, and LEDs that are all easy to position, I do not expect an issue wherever you place the connectors.
